title: Token Service · SLOs
description: SLIs, error budgets and burn rates for POST /token (availability and latency).

options.content:
**What users of an identity service feel:** can I get a token (availability), and is it fast (latency). Both are measured at the API for `POST /token`, the only public call.

- **SLI** = good events / all events. **SLO** = the target over a rolling window (`$window`). **Error budget** = what's allowed to go wrong (0.5% of calls for availability, 5% for latency).
- **Burn rate** = how fast the budget goes. 1× lasts exactly the window. Alerts are multi-window, multi-burn-rate (Google SRE workbook, chapter 5): 14.4× over 1 h and 5 m, 6× over 6 h and 30 m.
- Targets live in `deploy/helm/token-service/values.yaml` (`slo:`) and in this dashboard's hidden constants. Prometheus keeps 2 days on kind and 15 days in Compose, so the 30-day numbers cover what's stored.

| Budget left | What we do |
| --- | --- |
| over 50% | Ship as normal |
| 25–50% | Ship with care: smaller changes, watch the rollout |
| under 25% | Only fixes and reliability work |
| spent | Freeze features until it recovers; write a postmortem |

A page (fast or slow burn) always wins over the table: fix first.

panels.title: Availability SLO: 99.5% of POST /token calls without a 5xx, over the SLO window
Availability SLI ($window)
panels.description: Share of POST /token calls that didn't fail with a 5xx, over the whole SLO window ($window, or as much of it as Prometheus still keeps). 4xx answers (bad JWT, wrong scope, unknown user, rate limit) are the caller's problem and don't count.

panels.title: Error budget remaining ($window)
panels.description: How much of the window's error budget is left: 100% means no bad events, 0% means the SLO is missed for this window. Negative means it's overspent. The error budget policy below says what to do at each level.

panels.title: Burn rate (last 1 h)
panels.description: How fast the budget is being used right now. 1× uses exactly the whole budget by the end of the window. 6× over 6 h and 14.4× over 1 h are the alert thresholds.

panels.title: Bad events ($window)
panels.description: Number of calls that counted against this SLO in the window, so the percentages have a size next to them.

panels.title: SLO alerts firing
panels.description: Burn-rate alerts for this SLO that are firing now (Prometheus ALERTS). The rules only exist on Kubernetes (PrometheusRule); in Docker Compose this stays at 0.

panels.title: Availability SLI (5 m windows)
panels.description: The SLI per 5-minute window, against the objective (dashed line). Dips show when and how badly users were hit. Short dips are fine as long as the budget lasts.

panels.title: Error budget burndown (rolling $window)
panels.description: Budget left, recalculated over a rolling $window at each point. A steady line is healthy; a cliff is an incident. Below 0 the SLO is missed.

panels.title: Burn rate: fast (1 h) and slow (6 h)
panels.description: The two long windows the alerts use. Above 14.4× for an hour pages (2% of a 30-day budget gone per hour); above 6× for 6 hours pages too (5% gone in 6 hours). The short 5 m / 30 m windows make the alerts clear quickly once it's fixed.

panels.title: Latency SLO: 95% of POST /token calls under 0.5 s, over the SLO window
Latency SLI ($window)
panels.description: Share of POST /token calls answered within $lat_le s, over the whole SLO window ($window, or as much of it as Prometheus still keeps). Counts every answer, including 4xx.

panels.title: Error budget remaining ($window)
panels.description: How much of the window's error budget is left: 100% means no bad events, 0% means the SLO is missed for this window. Negative means it's overspent. The error budget policy below says what to do at each level.

panels.description: Burn-rate alerts for this SLO that are firing now (Prometheus ALERTS). The rules only exist on Kubernetes (PrometheusRule); in Docker Compose this stays at 0.

panels.description: The SLI per 5-minute window, against the objective (dashed line). Dips show when and how badly users were hit. Short dips are fine as long as the budget lasts.

panels.description: The two long windows the alerts use. Above 14.4× for an hour pages (2% of a 30-day budget gone per hour); above 6× for 6 hours pages too (5% gone in 6 hours). The short 5 m / 30 m windows make the alerts clear quickly once it's fixed.

panels.title: Burn rate per alert window (what the alerts look at)
Availability burn rate
panels.description: Burn rate in each window the alerts use. The fast-burn alert needs both 1h and 5m over 14.4×; the slow-burn alert needs both 6h and 30m over 6×.

panels.title: Latency burn rate
panels.description: Same windows for the latency SLO. Its alert (warning) needs both 1h and 5m over 14.4×.

panels.title: Context: what explains a burn (not counted in the SLOs)
Traffic by status class
panels.description: Event rate. A burn during low traffic can look scary but cost few calls; a small error ratio at peak can cost more. Read the SLI next to this.

panels.title: Caller errors (4xx) share
panels.description: 401/403/404/422/429 as a share of all calls. Not the service's fault, so not in the SLO, but for an identity service a jump usually means a misconfigured client, a key rotation gone wrong, or someone probing. Details on the Security & Auth dashboard.

panels.title: Latency percentiles vs target
panels.description: p50, p95 and p99 of POST /token. The latency SLO is met while p95 stays under the dashed $lat_le s line.

panels.title: Go service: failed mint RPCs by code
panels.description: gRPC calls to the Go service that didn't return OK. Unavailable or Internal here, with 5xx above, points at Redis or the Go pods.

panels.title: Postgres: pool timeouts and waits
panels.description: Requests that gave up waiting for a database connection (each is a 503), and the connections in use against the pool size.

panels.title: Redis: audit queue depth and pending
panels.description: Token events waiting in the Redis stream, and events delivered but not acknowledged. Growth here means the audit worker or Redis is struggling.
